one_liner: Aircall has a broad REST API with webhooks; customer admins self-generate an API ID/token (Basic auth) on a paid account, while OAuth is limited to Tech Partners. An MCP server is claimed but could not be verified from the supplied pages.
auth_notes: Basic Auth (api_id:api_token) is generated by an Aircall customer in Company Settings. OAuth 2.0 (authorization code) needs client_id/client_secret from Aircall via the Tech Partner program, so it is not self-serve. A multi-user toolkit would use per-customer Basic keys unless partnered.
access_notes: API credentials come from an existing Aircall customer account, and the pages say this starts with a paid account. The homepage offers a free trial, but no page confirms API keys work during the trial. Private-app keys need no review. Public OAuth apps need Tech Partner approval.
blocker_notes: A paid Aircall account is needed to generate keys. OAuth for multi-tenant use requires Tech Partner approval.

evidence.quote: Aircall Public API is a classic REST API.
We can call back any endpoint of your choice, each time an event occurs on an Aircall account
If you are an Aircall customer, building for your own Aircall account only, the Basic Auth flow will do the trick.
Before starting building the OAuth flow for your app, you will need to get OAuth client_id and client_secret from Aircall.
Getting API access starts with a paid Aircall account.
It's the fastest way to get started — no review process, no marketplace listing, and no OAuth flow required.
